units.name: globset
units.role: Compiles and matches sets of glob patterns (like .gitignore wildcards) against file paths.
units.description: This unit implements glob-pattern matching, the kind of wildcard syntax used in .gitignore files and shell filename expansion (e.g. "*.rs" or "src/**/*.txt"). It lets a caller compile one or many glob patterns into an efficient matcher and then, given a candidate file path, quickly find out which of those patterns match. It is pure, self-contained computation with no dependencies on any other unit in this repository; it reads no files and talks to no external systems itself.

entrypoints.name: Glob
entrypoints.plain: Represents one compiled glob pattern, e.g. "*.rs".

entrypoints.name: GlobBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures options (case sensitivity, path separators, etc.) before compiling a single glob pattern.

entrypoints.name: GlobMatcher
entrypoints.plain: A compiled single glob that can be tested against one candidate path at a time.

entrypoints.name: GlobSet
entrypoints.plain: A compiled collection of many globs that can all be matched against a path in one efficient pass.

entrypoints.name: GlobSetBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Accumulates individual Glob patterns and compiles them into a GlobSet.

entrypoints.name: Candidate
entrypoints.plain: A pre-processed path used to speed up matching the same path against many globs.

entrypoints.name: escape
entrypoints.plain: Escapes special glob characters in a literal string so it matches itself literally.

units.name: matcher
units.role: Defines the shared `Matcher` trait/vocabulary that every regex engine in this repo implements.
units.description: This unit defines a common abstraction, the Matcher trait, that describes what it means to be a line-oriented pattern-matching engine: finding matches, capturing groups, reporting match positions. It does not implement any regex engine itself; instead it is the shared contract that the Rust-regex-based engine, the PCRE2-based engine, and the search engine all agree to use, so that the rest of the program can be written generically against "some matcher" instead of a specific regex library. It performs no I/O of its own.

entrypoints.name: Matcher
entrypoints.plain: The trait a regex engine must implement to be usable for searching in ripgrep.

entrypoints.name: Match
entrypoints.plain: Represents the start/end byte offsets of a single match.

entrypoints.name: Captures
entrypoints.plain: Represents the capture groups produced by a single match, for replacement/highlighting.

entrypoints.name: NoError
entrypoints.plain: A placeholder error type used by matchers that can never fail.

entrypoints.name: LineTerminator
entrypoints.plain: Represents which byte (or byte pair) is treated as the end of a line.

units.name: cli-support
units.role: Grab-bag of OS/process/terminal utilities shared by search-oriented command-line tools.
units.description: This unit provides low-level operating-system and process utilities that a command-line search tool needs: reading patterns from files or stdin, escaping bytes for terminal display, parsing human-readable sizes like "10M", building a color-capable stdout writer, looking up the machine's hostname, and, most notably, transparently decompressing files (.gz, .bz2, .xz, .zst, etc.) by locating and running external decompression programs as subprocesses. It is the primary place in the codebase where ripgrep reaches outside its own process to run other programs.

entrypoints.name: DecompressionReader
entrypoints.plain: A streaming reader that transparently decompresses a file by piping it through an external program like gzip or xz.

entrypoints.name: DecompressionReaderBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures which decompression command to use for which file glob before building a DecompressionReader.

entrypoints.name: DecompressionMatcher
entrypoints.plain: Maps a file's name against globs like *.gz to decide which external decompression command applies.

entrypoints.name: CommandReader
entrypoints.plain: Spawns a child process and streams its stdout as a Read, surfacing stderr on failure.

entrypoints.name: resolve_binary
entrypoints.signature: pub fn resolve_binary<P: AsRef<Path>>(prog: P) -> Result<PathBuf, CommandError>
entrypoints.plain: Finds the absolute path of an external program by searching the PATH environment variable, to avoid unsafe relative-path execution on Windows.

entrypoints.name: hostname
entrypoints.plain: Returns the current machine's hostname, for use in things like file hyperlinks.

entrypoints.name: patterns_from_path
entrypoints.signature: pub fn patterns_from_path<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> io::Result<Vec<String>>
entrypoints.plain: Reads a file (e.g. given via -f/--file) and returns one search pattern per line.

entrypoints.name: patterns_from_stdin
entrypoints.plain: Reads search patterns, one per line, from standard input.

entrypoints.name: parse_human_readable_size
entrypoints.plain: Parses a human-friendly size string like "10M" into a byte count.

entrypoints.name: stdout
entrypoints.plain: Builds a stdout writer that supports colored/styled terminal output.

entrypoints.name: escape
entrypoints.plain: Escapes arbitrary bytes into a printable string for safe terminal/log display.

entrypoints.name: is_tty_stdin
entrypoints.plain: Reports whether stdin is connected to an interactive terminal.

effects.description: Spawns external decompression programs (gzip, bzip2, xz, lz4, brotli, zstd, uncompress) to decompress matching files; crates/cli/src/decompress.rs:490-531 defines the default commands and crates/cli/src/process.rs:104-118 (CommandReaderBuilder::build) actually spawns the child process.
Reads the PATH environment variable to resolve an external program's absolute path before executing it (crates/cli/src/decompress.rs:462).
Opens files directly when no decompression is needed (crates/cli/src/decompress.rs:362, new_passthru) and reads pattern files from disk (crates/cli/src/pattern.rs:82-103).
Queries the OS for the machine hostname via libc::gethostname on Unix or the Windows computer-name API (crates/cli/src/hostname.rs:16-75).
Detects whether stdin/stdout/stderr are connected to a terminal (crates/cli/src/lib.rs:170-292).

units.name: regex-engine
units.role: Adapts Rust's own `regex`/`regex-automata` engine to the shared Matcher interface.
units.description: This unit lets ripgrep search using Rust's native regular expression syntax. It translates a user's pattern string into the internal representation used by the `regex-automata` engine, applies ripgrep-specific transformations (such as literal-string extraction for fast pre-filtering, smart case handling, and detecting patterns that can never match), and exposes the whole thing through the shared Matcher trait so the rest of the program can use it generically. It is pure computation over in-memory strings and bytes; it performs no I/O.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcher
entrypoints.plain: A compiled Rust-syntax regex that implements the shared Matcher trait.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures options (case-insensitivity, multi-line, word boundaries, etc.) before compiling a RegexMatcher.

entrypoints.name: RegexCaptures
entrypoints.plain: Holds the capture groups from a single match made by RegexMatcher.

entrypoints.name: Error
entrypoints.plain: Describes why a pattern failed to compile (bad syntax, unsupported feature, etc.).

units.name: pcre2-engine
units.role: Adapts the native PCRE2 C library (backreferences, lookaround) to the shared Matcher interface.
units.description: This unit gives ripgrep an optional second regex engine, PCRE2, which supports features Rust's own regex engine deliberately omits, such as backreferences and lookaround assertions. It is a thin wrapper around the external `pcre2` crate (which itself links the native PCRE2 C library and can use its JIT compiler) so that PCRE2 patterns can be used anywhere the shared Matcher trait is expected. This unit is only compiled in when ripgrep's optional "pcre2" feature is enabled.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcher
entrypoints.plain: A compiled PCRE2 regex that implements the shared Matcher trait.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures PCRE2-specific options before compiling a RegexMatcher.

entrypoints.name: RegexCaptures
entrypoints.plain: Holds the capture groups from a single PCRE2 match.

entrypoints.name: is_jit_available
entrypoints.plain: Reports whether PCRE2's just-in-time compiler is available on this build/platform.

effects.description: Links and calls into the native PCRE2 C library (via the external `pcre2` crate), including its optional JIT compiler, through unsafe FFI rather than any I/O.

units.name: searcher
units.role: The core line-oriented search engine: reads bytes from a source and reports matches to a Sink.
units.description: This is ripgrep's core search engine. Given a Matcher (a compiled regex) and a source of bytes (a file or an in-memory slice), it decides how to consume that data efficiently, including deciding whether to memory-map the file, detecting binary content, counting lines, handling multi-line patterns, and gathering context lines around a match. It reports what it finds to a caller-supplied Sink, which is how results eventually reach a printer or any other consumer. It does not decide how results look on screen, only how the search itself is executed.

entrypoints.name: Searcher
entrypoints.plain: Executes a search of a byte source using a Matcher, reporting results to a Sink.

entrypoints.name: SearcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures search behavior (context lines, binary detection, multi-line mode, memory-map policy) before building a Searcher.

entrypoints.name: Sink
entrypoints.plain: The trait a caller implements to receive search results (matches, context lines, start/end events) as they are found.

entrypoints.name: MmapChoice
entrypoints.plain: Controls whether the searcher is allowed to memory-map files instead of reading them into a buffer.

entrypoints.name: BinaryDetection
entrypoints.plain: Configures how the searcher decides a file is binary and what to do about it (skip vs. treat first NUL byte as end of data).

effects.description: Optionally memory-maps files instead of reading them, via crates/searcher/src/searcher/mmap.rs:49-100 (MmapChoice::auto / Mmap::map), which the caller must opt into as `unsafe` because the file could change underneath the mapping.

units.name: printer
units.role: Formats search results (produced by the searcher) into grep-style, JSON, or summary output.
units.description: This unit turns raw search matches into the text ripgrep actually shows the user. It implements the searcher's Sink trait three different ways: a classic colored grep-style printer, a machine-readable JSON-lines printer, and a summary printer that reports counts and matched/unmatched file lists. It also handles coloring, terminal hyperlinks to matched files, and aggregate statistics like elapsed time. It writes only to a generic writer supplied by its caller (typically stdout), so it does not itself decide where output ultimately goes.

entrypoints.name: Standard
entrypoints.plain: Prints matches in the traditional colored grep-like format.

entrypoints.name: StandardBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures the Standard printer (colors, line numbers, context, replacement, hyperlinks) before building it.

entrypoints.name: JSON
entrypoints.plain: Prints matches as a stream of JSON-lines messages for machine consumption.

entrypoints.name: Summary
entrypoints.plain: Prints aggregate results such as match counts or matched file names only.

entrypoints.name: Stats
entrypoints.plain: Accumulates search statistics (matches, lines, bytes, elapsed time) across one or more searches.

entrypoints.name: ColorSpecs
entrypoints.plain: Defines what colors/styles to use for matched text, line numbers, paths, etc.

entrypoints.name: HyperlinkConfig
entrypoints.plain: Configures the terminal hyperlink format (e.g. file://hostname/path) used to link matched lines back to files.

effects.description: Records wall-clock timing for a search using std::time::Instant::now() to report elapsed time in Stats output (e.g. crates/printer/src/standard.rs:529, crates/printer/src/json.rs:513, crates/printer/src/summary.rs:406).

units.name: ignore
units.role: Recursively walks directory trees while applying .gitignore-style filtering rules, in parallel.
units.description: This unit is ripgrep's file-discovery engine. It recursively walks a directory tree, deciding for each entry whether it should be skipped based on .gitignore files, .ignore files, global git excludes, explicit type filters (like "only .rs files"), and explicit include/exclude overrides given on the command line. It can do this walk single-threaded or in parallel across many worker threads for speed. Secondarily it exposes its glob and gitignore matching logic standalone for callers that just need the filtering rules without the directory walk itself.

entrypoints.name: WalkBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures directory-walking options (hidden files, ignore files, filters, depth) before building a Walk or WalkParallel.

entrypoints.name: Walk
entrypoints.plain: A single-threaded iterator over directory entries that respects ignore rules.

entrypoints.name: WalkParallel
entrypoints.plain: A multi-threaded directory walker that invokes a caller-supplied visitor for each entry.

entrypoints.name: DirEntry
entrypoints.plain: Represents one file or directory found during the walk, including its path and metadata.

entrypoints.name: Gitignore
entrypoints.plain: A compiled set of gitignore-style rules parsed from one file, usable to test whether a path is ignored.

entrypoints.name: GitignoreBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Parses gitignore-style rule lines and compiles them into a Gitignore matcher.

entrypoints.name: gitconfig_excludes_path
entrypoints.plain: Determines the path to git's global excludes file, e.g. from core.excludesFile or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore.

entrypoints.name: Types
entrypoints.plain: A compiled set of named file-type definitions (e.g. "rust" -> *.rs) used for --type filtering.

entrypoints.name: TypesBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Accumulates file-type definitions and compiles them into Types.

entrypoints.name: Override
entrypoints.plain: A compiled set of explicit include/exclude glob overrides, e.g. from -g/--glob flags.

effects.description: Recursively reads directory entries and the contents of .gitignore/.ignore/.git/info/exclude files while walking a directory tree (crates/ignore/src/dir.rs, crates/ignore/src/walk.rs).

Reads XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HOME/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM and the current directory to locate the global gitignore (core.excludesFile), crates/ignore/src/gitignore.rs:142,607-703; also reads the current directory while walking (crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:1082).
Spawns and coordinates a pool of worker threads (via crossbeam-deque) to walk directory trees in parallel (WalkParallel, crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:1411).

units.name: index
units.role: Builds and queries a persistent on-disk search index to speed up repeated searches (unstable, opt-in).
units.description: This unit is an experimental, opt-in feature (gated behind the `unstable-index` Cargo feature and explicitly documented as possibly having serious bugs) that builds a persistent, on-disk index of file contents using an embedded database, so that repeated searches over the same directory can skip files that provably cannot match a pattern. It extracts required literal substrings from a compiled regex to decide what to look up in the index. It is otherwise independent of the rest of the workspace: it has no path dependency on any other crate in this repository.

entrypoints.name: Index
entrypoints.plain: An open handle to an on-disk search index that can be queried.

entrypoints.name: IndexBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Builds a new on-disk index by scanning and recording file contents.

entrypoints.name: IndexDiscovery
entrypoints.plain: Locates an existing on-disk index associated with a directory, if one exists.

effects.description: Reads and writes an embedded on-disk database (via the `redb` crate) that stores the persistent search index, and uses `fst` finite-state-transducer files for compact literal lookups (crates/index/src/index.rs).
Creates, opens, and reads index files stored on disk (crates/index/src/index.rs:53, std::fs::create_dir).

Reads the current working directory and a configurable environment variable to help locate the index (crates/index/src/index.rs:124, std::env::current_dir; crates/index/src/index.rs:132, std::env::var_os).

units.name: grep-facade
units.role: A thin re-export facade that bundles the cli/matcher/pcre2/printer/regex/searcher units under one crate.
units.description: This unit contains no logic of its own. It exists purely so that a downstream consumer, in this case ripgrep's own command-line binary, can depend on a single crate (`grep`) instead of naming every individual sub-crate. It simply re-exports the cli-support, matcher, pcre2-engine (optional), printer, regex-engine, and searcher units as named sub-modules. Every effect and dependency it appears to have is really an effect or dependency of whichever re-exported unit is actually used.

entrypoints.name: cli
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_cli as cli;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the cli-support unit as `grep::cli`.

entrypoints.name: matcher
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_matcher as matcher;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the matcher unit as `grep::matcher`.

entrypoints.name: pcre2
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_pcre2 as pcre2;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the pcre2-engine unit as `grep::pcre2`, only when the "pcre2" feature is enabled.

entrypoints.name: printer
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_printer as printer;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the printer unit as `grep::printer`.

entrypoints.name: regex
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_regex as regex;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the regex-engine unit as `grep::regex`.

entrypoints.name: searcher
entrypoints.signature: pub extern crate grep_searcher as searcher;
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the searcher unit as `grep::searcher`.

units.name: core
units.role: The `rg` command-line application: parses flags, drives the directory walk and search, and prints results/errors.
units.description: This is the ripgrep application itself, built as the `rg` binary. It parses command-line flags and an optional config file into a structured configuration, decides which mode to run in (search, list files, list types, generate help/man-page/shell-completions, or use the experimental index), builds and drives the directory walk and search (single- or multi-threaded), wires together the ignore, regex, searcher, and printer units according to the user's flags, and reports errors and summary statistics. It is the glue layer that turns everything the other units provide into a working command-line tool, and it is also where most of the program's direct interaction with the outside world (besides file searching itself) happens.

entrypoints.name: main
entrypoints.plain: The `rg` program's entrypoint: parses arguments and runs ripgrep, returning the process exit code.

entrypoints.name: parse
entrypoints.plain: Reads argv (and the RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH config file, if set) and turns it into ripgrep's resolved configuration, or a request to print help/version/etc.

entrypoints.name: run
entrypoints.plain: Given parsed configuration, dispatches to the appropriate mode: search, list files, list types, index, or generate output.

entrypoints.name: search
entrypoints.plain: Runs a single-threaded recursive search over the configured directory/files and prints results.

entrypoints.name: search_parallel
entrypoints.plain: Runs a multi-threaded recursive search, parallelizing over the directory walk.

entrypoints.name: SearchWorker
entrypoints.plain: Searches one file, choosing whether to decompress it, run it through a --pre preprocessor command, or search it directly.

entrypoints.name: config::args
entrypoints.plain: Reads the RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH environment variable and, if set, loads extra command-line arguments from that config file.

entrypoints.name: HiArgs
entrypoints.plain: The fully-resolved configuration derived from CLI flags, used to build the walker, matcher, searcher, and printer.

entrypoints.name: generate_man_page
entrypoints.plain: Generates ripgrep's man page text, used by `rg --generate man` and packaging scripts.

effects.description: Reads RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH to locate an optional config file (crates/core/flags/config.rs:17), argv via std::env::args_os (crates/core/flags/parse.rs:72,103), the current executable path (crates/core/flags/lowargs.rs:693-711), and PWD / WSL_DISTRO_NAME while resolving the current working directory (crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs:1335-1442).

Opens and reads the ripgrep config file from disk (crates/core/flags/config.rs:67), opens files to feed the --pre preprocessor (crates/core/search.rs:304), and stats/reads file metadata for each candidate file during search (crates/core/haystack.rs:60-153).

Directly spawns an arbitrary external command for the --pre preprocessor flag (crates/core/search.rs:303 and crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs:1373, std::process::Command::new), and drives the cli-support unit's decompression subprocesses for compressed files (crates/core/search.rs:73,237,263).
Measures wall-clock elapsed time for a search using std::time::Instant, to print summary statistics (crates/core/main.rs:114,169,446).

Writes all program output, error messages, and log lines to stdout/stderr, and terminates the process with a specific exit code via std::process::exit / ExitCode (crates/core/messages.rs:27-67, crates/core/main.rs:44-107).

units.name: build-script
units.role: Cargo build script that embeds the current git commit hash and Windows executable options into the `rg` binary.
units.description: This is a Cargo build script that runs at compile time, before the `rg` binary itself is compiled. It shells out to the `git` command to capture the current commit hash and exposes it to the program as a compile-time environment variable (used in ripgrep's --version output), and, on Windows with the MSVC toolchain, embeds an application manifest (for long file path support) and tightens linker warnings into errors. It has no runtime relationship with the rest of the application; it only affects how the `rg` binary is built.

entrypoints.name: main
entrypoints.plain: The build script's entrypoint, invoked by Cargo before compiling the `rg` binary.

entrypoints.name: set_git_revision_hash
entrypoints.plain: Runs `git rev-parse --short=10 HEAD` and exposes the result as the RIPGREP_BUILD_GIT_HASH compile-time environment variable.

entrypoints.name: set_windows_exe_options
entrypoints.plain: On Windows/MSVC builds, embeds pkg/windows/Manifest.xml into the binary and turns linker warnings into errors.

effects.description: Runs the external `git` command (`git rev-parse --short=10 HEAD`) to determine the current commit hash (build.rs:36-41).
Reads CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS and CARGO_CFG_TARGET_ENV to decide whether to apply Windows-specific linker options (build.rs:15-19).
Reads the current working directory and reasons about the path to pkg/windows/Manifest.xml (build.rs:21-23).
